marrow__ANAT_CH27_Q015.takeaway: Cauda equina syndrome often causes asymmetric lower-limb weakness, unlike symmetric conus medullaris syndrome.
marrow__ANAT_CH27_Q015.displayText: The scenario describes cauda equina syndrome. Conus medullaris syndrome typically shows symmetrical weakness of the lower limbs, whereas cauda equina syndrome typically shows asymmetrical weakness. Radicular pain, lower motor-neuron injury and urinary retention may occur in both conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes.
emphasis: symmetrical weakness of the lower limbs

rationales.a: Radicular pain is common in cauda equina syndrome.
rationales.b: Cauda equina lesions damage lower motor neurons.
rationales.d: Urinary retention may occur in cauda equina syndrome; symmetric weakness is more characteristic of conus medullaris syndrome.
